stance_summary: Treat the manuscript as a diagnosis problem: find the cheapest test that tells whether the failure is missing evidence, wrong category, or weak packaging.
anchored_assumption: Disambiguation question: is the manuscript actually broken because it lacks a falsifiable measurable claim, or because the five-layer wiki system is being submitted under the wrong article category despite having a usable methods contribution?

candidates.one_line: Run a traceability audit on one existing high-value artifact and make the paper's claim narrower: the system preserves source provenance in real nuclear-physics writing.
candidates.first_concrete_step: Today, take the existing 58-page review draft citation ledger and compute a three-bin table: wiki-backed, external-discovered, unresolved, with 10 randomly selected entries manually spot-checked against their source pages.
candidates.cost_estimate: 6-10 hours for the audit table and manuscript insertion; 2-3 days if the ledger needs cleanup.
candidates.info_gain: If it works, the manuscript gains a falsifiable result without a human-subject study. If it fails, the current evidence base is too anecdotal and the article should not be sold as original research.
candidates.risk: The ledger may be incomplete or inconsistent, causing the test to collapse into cleanup; worst-case time loss is one day.

orthogonality_to_tried.difference: T1 only states examples; this measures provenance on an existing artifact.
It does not ask the journal to accept an experience report.
No self-graded questions; the units are existing citations and source links.
No editor query.
It adds a small original audit, not a broad review expansion.
It tests provenance quality, not commit-level replay reproducibility.

candidates.dependencies: Requires the existing review draft, citation ledger, and wiki source pages to be locally available.

candidates.one_line: Ablate the weakest component by removing efficiency language and recasting the contribution as a static, testable knowledge-schema design for nuclear theory workflows.
candidates.first_concrete_step: Today, rewrite the abstract's Results sentence into one schema claim and one static inventory claim, then delete any sentence that implies speedup, productivity, or model improvement.
candidates.cost_estimate: 4-6 hours for the ablation pass; 1-2 days to rebalance the manuscript to 5000-8000 chars.
candidates.info_gain: If the manuscript still reads like a contribution, the core problem was overclaiming. If it becomes empty, the five-layer architecture has no publishable claim without data.
candidates.risk: The paper may become too descriptive for an original article; worst-case time loss is half a day before abandoning this route.

orthogonality_to_tried.difference: It changes the claim surface rather than padding the existing draft.
It frames a schema/methods article, not a practice report.
It avoids invented validation and only preserves static verifiable claims.
No editor query.
It shrinks and sharpens the manuscript instead of expanding into a review.
It changes article claim type, not reproducibility evidence.

candidates.dependencies: Needs only the current manuscript and willingness to cut claims that cannot be verified.

candidates.one_line: Use past Nuclear Techniques articles as the venue unit test: determine whether a methods-style infrastructure paper without controlled experiments is a known accepted form.
candidates.first_concrete_step: Today, build a 10-row table from recent Nuclear Techniques AI/special-topic papers with columns: article type, evidence type, data/experiment present, word length class, and closest match to this manuscript.
candidates.cost_estimate: 3-5 hours for the venue table; one day to adjust positioning if a close precedent exists.
candidates.info_gain: If a close precedent exists, the problem is packaging and genre language. If none exists, the current article must either add real evidence or become a review.
candidates.risk: Public pages may not expose enough full text quickly; worst-case time loss is one afternoon.

orthogonality_to_tried.difference: It tests venue fit rather than manuscript completeness.
It does not rely on a rejected experience-report category.
No new experiment or self-grading.
It uses public precedent, not editor permission.
It may justify original-article packaging without review expansion.
It tests journal genre constraints, not system reproducibility.

candidates.dependencies: Requires public access to recent Nuclear Techniques articles or downloaded PDFs.

candidates.one_line: Convert one manuscript claim into a static lint benchmark over the existing wikis: the architecture makes stale links, orphan pages, and missing provenance mechanically discoverable.
candidates.first_concrete_step: Today, run the existing wiki lint or git-backed index check once and extract only objective counts: broken links, orphan pages, stale frontmatter, and resolved findings from the last report.
candidates.cost_estimate: 4-8 hours if the lint pipeline already runs; 2 days if report parsing needs manual cleanup.
candidates.info_gain: If objective defects and fixes are recoverable, the paper gains an engineering validation that matches its governance claims. If not, the governance section is aspirational and should be shortened.
candidates.risk: The lint report may mix private and public material or be too wiki-specific; worst-case time loss is one day.

orthogonality_to_tried.difference: It adds objective maintenance data rather than descriptive inventory.
It supports a methods/tooling claim, not a practice narrative.
No human scoring; counts come from static checks.
No editor query.
It avoids agent-literature expansion and stays evidence-first.
It validates maintainability, not replay of a single answer.

candidates.dependencies: Requires existing lint reports or scripts and careful exclusion of confidential review material.

candidates.one_line: Make the negative result explicit: test whether the current wiki can support an AI-agent review section, and if it cannot, use that as a boundary condition rather than filling it with shallow citations.
candidates.first_concrete_step: Today, write a one-page appendix-style table listing the 11 current agent references with status columns: in wiki, read depth, supports which sentence, and must-keep or removable.
candidates.cost_estimate: 3-6 hours for the table; 1 day to prune or quarantine unsupported claims.
candidates.info_gain: If most references support precise claims, the intro can stay. If not, the manuscript should stop pretending to review AI agents and present them only as minimal background.
candidates.risk: This may reveal that the opening literature frame is thin; worst-case time loss is half a day and a shorter, more honest introduction.

orthogonality_to_tried.difference: It stress-tests the current reference frame rather than accepting it.
It does not change into a practice report.
No new self-generated performance evidence.
No editor query.
It rejects broad agent-literature expansion unless the current claims require it.
It audits citation support, not reproducibility.

candidates.dependencies: Requires only the current 11 references and local notes; no more than two new papers if a crucial citation is missing.

convergence_note: The other solver may also propose B3, because venue-precedent testing is the cheapest way to separate category failure from evidence failure.
